title: About Me drafting moved from per-editor AI Write to Professor Mari
reality: v2.3.2 (Changed) moved Conversation About Me drafting from per-editor AI Write controls to Professor Mari. Character and Persona Convo editors no longer expose a separate model connection or source settings; Mari inspects the saved character/persona, writes the bio in their voice, and saves it directly to the real About Me field. (The v2.3.0 #3646 fix to AI Write macro resolution is superseded by this removal.) 2.3.0 also notes the About Me profile and update_about_me tool remain built into the Engine, not downloadable agents.
fix: Rewrite the `aboutMe` bullet in the Conversation-mode Profile section (references/character-cards.md, ~line 103): drop the gear-icon source picker / per-editor AI Write / separate model connection description and state that AI drafting is now done by asking Professor Mari, who writes in the character's voice and saves to the real aboutMe field. Mark `aboutMeSources` in the schema block (~line 55) as legacy/no longer surfaced in the editors. Keep the per-chat about-me override bullet as-is.

title: Bot Browser renamed to Card Browser / Download Cards / Cards Library
reality: v2.3.0 (Changed) renamed Bot Browser to Card Browser throughout the UI, docs, onboarding, and Mari guidance, and renamed Browse Online to Download Cards; a v2.3.0 fix unified the online Card Browser with the Character/Persona/Agent library shell, opening as 'Cards Library' with 'Browse character cards online'. v2.3.1 further hardened Card Browser catalog requests.
fix: In the Import/Export section (~line 182), replace 'searchable from the in-app Bot Browser' with the Card Browser naming: sidebar action is 'Download Cards', it opens as the 'Cards Library' using the shared library shell. Grep the whole skill for other 'Bot Browser'/'Browse Online' occurrences and rename.

title: Mari/app-data card updates now preserve unrelated fields (#3708)
reality: v2.3.2 (Fixed, #3708) preserved greetings, example dialogue, creator notes, system prompts, post-history instructions, character versions, and alternate greetings when Professor Mari or another app-data caller updates an unrelated Character Card field. Before 2.3.2, such updates could wipe those fields. Related: v2.3.0 (#3674) fixed Mari blank character-generation turns and normalized common character-card field names.
fix: Add a note in the Professor Mari Pattern section (near the character.create/update discussion): as of v2.3.2 (#3708) Mari's card updates are field-safe — editing one field no longer clobbers greetings, mes_example, creator_notes, system_prompt, post_history_instructions, character_version, or alternate_greetings; on earlier versions users should re-check those fields after a Mari edit.

title: Sprite transparency: native-alpha-first pipeline missing
reality: v2.3.0 (Changed) reworked Character and Persona sprite transparency around a native-alpha-first pipeline: providers that cannot return transparent PNGs get a subject-aware saturated chroma matte, then border-connected soft matting and color despill; the optional neural background remover is reserved for genuinely complex backgrounds; saved legacy white-background sprites remain cleanable with restore points.
fix: In the Sprite System section (~line 190), add the v2.3.0 transparency pipeline: generated sprites prefer native alpha; fallback is chroma matte + soft matting + despill; neural remover is only for complex backgrounds; legacy white-background sprites can still be cleaned with restore points.

title: Avatar upload/replace field above Name in Character Metadata
reality: v2.3.3 (Fixed) added a clearly labeled avatar upload/replace field above Name in Character Metadata, reusing the editor-portrait upload and crop flow, discoverable on desktop and touch. The skill (~line 96) currently describes the metadata block as leading with Title/comment directly below Name.
fix: Update the metadata-layout sentence (~line 96): the primary identity block now starts with an avatar upload/replace field above Name (v2.3.3, same upload/crop flow as the editor portrait), then Name, then the Title/comment field.

title: Personas gained Open Full Library
reality: v2.3.0 (Added) gave Personas an 'Open Full Library' with the same responsive card grid, search, sorting, preview pane, paging, scroll restoration, and editor return flow as the Character Library.
fix: In the Character vs. Persona section (or a short UI note), add that Personas now have Open Full Library (v2.3.0) mirroring the Character full library: card grid, search, sorting, preview pane, paging, scroll restoration, editor return flow.

title: <START> example-dialogue separator survives XML sanitization
reality: v2.3.0 (Fixed, #3623) preserved the standard <START> example-dialogue separator through XML prompt sanitization, including cards whose importer had already encoded the marker, without letting other XML-looking card text through unescaped.
fix: In the mes_example guidance (schema table and/or Common Mistakes), note that the standard <START> separator in mes_example is safe: since v2.3.0 (#3623) XML sanitization preserves it (even importer-encoded), while other XML-looking card text is still escaped.

title: Prompt macros resolved at final provider boundary (#3704)
reality: v2.3.2 (Fixed, #3704) resolves {{user}}, {{char}}, and other prompt macros in opening greetings and /guided instructions at the final provider boundary, including lorebook routing and embedding scans, so late prompt injections can no longer send raw identity placeholders to models.
fix: In the Character vs. Persona paragraph about {{user}} substitution (~line 94) or the Conversation macros section, add that since v2.3.2 (#3704) macro resolution happens at the final provider boundary — first_mes/alternate greetings and /guided text are guaranteed resolved, including in lorebook routing and embedding scans.

title: Character-panel filters are session-only since 2.3.3
reality: v2.3.3 (Fixed) reset stale Character-panel search, tag, favorite, and scroll filters during the update and made them session-only, so reopening Marinara shows the full Character collection instead of an old filtered subset; Full Library sorting and position preferences remain persisted.
fix: Add a brief note (Characters Panel / troubleshooting context): as of v2.3.3, Character-panel search/tag/favorite/scroll filters do not persist across app restarts (session-only); only Full Library sorting/position preferences persist. Useful when users report 'missing' characters caused by stale filters on older versions.

title: Roleplay chats stay Persona-less when no Persona selected
reality: v2.3.2 (Fixed) kept new Roleplay chats Persona-less when the user selects no Persona — including the first optimistic message snapshot, provider prompt, scene generation, and combat context; only Conversation mode may fall back to the globally active Persona.
fix: In the Character vs. Persona section, qualify the persona-injection claim: since v2.3.2, only Conversation mode falls back to the globally active Persona; a Roleplay chat created with no Persona selected remains persona-less throughout prompting.

title: Conversation Calls is now an optional downloadable package ('Calls')
reality: v2.3.0 (Added/Changed) moved Conversation audio/video calls into an optional downloadable package with a package-owned server runtime; Local Whisper became a Calls-owned download (uninstalling Calls removes Whisper models). v2.3.2 (#3676) renamed user-facing references to 'Calls' (package IDs/legacy symbols preserved). The skill's 'Sprites → Clips (Video-Call Presence)' and in-call command sections, plus phoneticName ('Conversation Call TTS'), describe calls as built-in.
fix: In the Sprites → Clips / Character Video Presence / in-call commands sections and the phoneticName bullet, note that as of v2.3.0 calls are the optional downloadable 'Calls' package (renamed from Conversation Calls in v2.3.2) — the Sprites → Clips call features, [custom_clip]/[react:] in-call commands, and call TTS phonetics only apply when the Calls package is installed, and cited conversation-calls route/service paths are now package-owned rather than base-Engine code.
